chunks.content: Helix Labs was founded in Rotterdam in 2019 by Dr. Sarah Chen, a biochemist who had spent the previous decade at Delft University of Technology. The company set out to build a portable sequencer cheap enough for field clinics. Sarah Chen had argued for years that the bottleneck in genomics was not the chemistry but the logistics.

Helix Labs shipped its first prototype, called Helix, to three clinics in 2021. It was slower than a benchtop machine and it was noisy, but it weighed under two kilograms and ran for six hours on a battery. Marcus Webb, who joined Helix Labs as chief scientist in 2020, rebuilt the basecaller inside Helix twice in eighteen months.

Orbit Biosciences had been working on the same problem since 2016, with far more money and a larger team. Sarah Chen had in fact left Orbit Biosciences to start Helix Labs, taking two engineers with her. For four years the two companies competed for the same grants and the same customers.

Priya Raman ran the field programme from Rotterdam. Between 2021 and 2023 she placed Helix units in clinics across four countries, and it was her data, not the laboratory benchmarks, that convinced the regulators. Priya Raman reported directly to Dr. Sarah Chen.

In March 2023 Helix Labs merged with Orbit Biosciences. The merged company kept the Helix name for the device and the Orbit Biosciences name for the business. Marcus Webb left within the year; Priya Raman stayed on to run the combined field programme.

Delft University of Technology retained a small equity stake in Helix Labs from the founding, and two of its laboratories continued to test the Helix in the field. Dr. Sarah Chen returned to Delft as a visiting professor in 2024, while remaining on the board of Orbit Biosciences.
